p1280.title: fix: autofix jobs approve the runs their GITHUB_TOKEN push leaves holding
p1280.body:
After `closures-autofix`/`claims-autofix` push with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the
`pull_request` runs that push triggers sit `action_required` for a human and
shadow the dispatched greens on the PR (measured tonight, #1276). This branch
adds one approve STEP to each of the two existing jobs — not a third job
(`.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md`, "add no third job") — that clears those holds
itself, and adds one sentence to that rule describing the step.

**Round 1 (#1280: `dead-approve-step`) is repaired at this head.** The
`HPO_APPROVER_*` → `HPO_RUNS_*` rename had replaced the guards and the
messages but not the PEM write: `printf '%s\n' "$APPROVER_PEM" > "$key"` put
one newline in the key file, real openssl refused to sign it, and both steps
could only ever reach the signing-failure warning and exit 0 — a dead approve
step green behind a transient-reading warning. The round-0 harness missed it
because its stub `openssl` (copied from `app_approve.sh`'s self-test shape)
checked only that the key file was non-empty, never its content. Both sites
now write `$RUNS_PEM`, and the re-verification below runs the committed step
bodies against a REAL throwaway RSA key with real openssl, only `curl`
stubbed — plus the old body as the failing control.

**The step's shape** (identical in both jobs, between the push step and the
`always()` report step, which stays last):

- Gated on a new `token_push` output the push step sets only after a real
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` push (the `CLOSURES_PUSH_TOKEN` PAT path and the
  nothing-staged path both exit before it), so the approve step never runs
  when no hold was created.
- **Fully fail-soft while the secrets are absent**: no `HPO_RUNS_PEM` → one
  `::notice::` line, exit 0, nothing minted, nothing approved, no summary
  write — until the owner sets the secrets, job behavior is unchanged. No
  `HPO_RUNS_APPID` → one `::warning::` line, same exit 0.
- **When present**: mints the installation token of a dedicated Actions-only
  App (Actions: write alone — a deliberately smaller blast radius than
  `hpo-approver`) by porting `tools/audit/app_approve.sh`'s RS256 flow inline:
  JWT (`iss` = the App id from `HPO_RUNS_APPID`, iat −60 / exp +540, same as
  the script) signed with `openssl dgst -sha256 -sign` against the PEM
  written from the `RUNS_PEM` secret env to a umask-077 file under
  `$RUNNER_TEMP`; the JWT and token live only in mode-600 header files, never
  on a command line, never printed, `{ set +x; }` first as in
  `app_approve.sh`; an EXIT trap revokes the token
  (`DELETE /installation/token`) and removes the files on every path, and —
  as of the round-1 repair — `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP` makes that EXIT
  trap fire on job cancellation too (app_approve.sh's bounded-gap line). It
  then lists
  `/repos/<repo>/actions/runs?branch=<head_ref>&status=action_required`,
  POSTs `/repos/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>/approve` for every run found, and
  appends the after-state to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in the fenced-block shape
  `autofix-report` uses.
- **Fail-soft after the push too, deliberately**: a mint or approve error
  warns and exits 0 rather than reddening the job, because a red autofix job
  means "no bot commit" (#523) and the commit exists; the summary line stays
  the job's signal.

**Scope note (mid-fix change) — and the operational state as of handoff.**
The dedicated minimal App is **live**: the secrets `HPO_RUNS_PEM` /
`HPO_RUNS_APPID` are set and bound to the **hpo-runs** App (id 5009497,
installation 163211961, token permissions verified `actions: write` only —
the blast-radius decision); the interim `HPO_APPROVER_*` pair is deleted,
and the step fires for real on the next bot push. Local key material for
future sessions: `~/.zcode/hpo-runs.pem` and `~/.zcode/hpo-run.appid` —
note the **singular "run" in the appid filename** (the owner saved it that
way); the workflow reads only the SECRETS, so the filename does not matter,
recorded here so the next session does not "fix" it. Earlier drafts of this
branch read `HPO_APPROVER_*`; renamed on the coordinator's instruction.
Until a branch's runtime has both secrets (now: it does), the step is a
no-op notice — that fail-soft default stays for any future secret outage.

**Policy note — the owner's review merges this:** `.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md`
is a CODEOWNERS path (`/.claude/rules/ @tvofi`), so this pull request cannot
merge without the owner's approving review on GitHub (decision 0009 step 6).
The one-sentence rule addition stays within the file's 96-line
`policy_budgets.json` cap — no cap was raised — and deliberately names no
secret: it reads "fail-soft while its secrets are absent", because a secret
name in policy rots on rotation (the interim pair was deleted today).

## Head

5258bd2b2bf34b3a120474aabf35a2b3ca3ab488 (round-1 repair on ca0d196, then the
rule-sentence de-naming on e71ba6e; every figure below names the commit it ran
at where that matters — the workflow figures are at e71ba6e and are untouched
by 5258bd2, which changed only the rule sentence and its generated mirror)

## Mutation proof

n/a: a GitHub workflow step has no local test harness — the YAML only
executes in Actions, so no local check can go red on a mutated step. What IS
verified, all against step bodies extracted from the COMMITTED YAML (`git
show <rev>:.github/workflows/tests.yml`, parsed, `[0]['run']` — not a hand
copy):

- The round-1 defect reproduced as the mutation control: the round-0 body
  (extracted at ca0d196) run with a REAL throwaway RSA key and REAL openssl
  reaches exactly `::warning::signing the run-approver App JWT failed` and
  exits 0 having approved nothing (figure B) — the one-line variable repair
  at e71ba6e flips that to sign-mint-approve (figure C). That is the
  fix's load-bearing line, broken and restored.
- `bash -n` clean on every step body of both jobs; `yaml.safe_load` parses;
  step order in both jobs is push → Approve → report, report still
  `if: always()` and last; both approve steps contain
  `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP` and no `$APPROVER_*` reference
  (`grep -c APPROVER .github/workflows/tests.yml` → 0).
- The mint flow dry-checked with only `curl` stubbed (installation id 99,
  stub token, two held runs then none): real key, real openssl, real
  python3/bash — signs, mints, approves, mode-600 headers, trap revokes,
  zero leaks (figure C).
- The closest local analogue to a listing mutation: stub listing returns 500
  → zero approve POSTs and a `::warning::listing ... failed` line instead —
  the step approves exactly what it finds, nothing else.

## Null control

- **Unchanged-behavior claim**: with `HPO_RUNS_PEM` unset, executing the
  committed step body prints exactly one notice line and touches nothing
  (figure A) — that IS the control for "until the owner sets the secrets,
  behavior is unchanged".
- **Real-signing control**: figure C's JWT, captured from the header file the
  curl stub copied, verifies `Verified OK` under
  `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` against the throwaway PUBLIC key — the
  signature is genuinely the real key's, not stub text; its payload reads
  `{"iat":...,"exp":...,"iss":"424242"}`, so the App id flows from
  `RUNS_APPID`, and the header is `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}`.
- **Leak-grep control**: the stub revoke endpoint greps the token header file
  for the stub token and fails on a miss — the single logged
  `curl installation/token` proves the header file genuinely carried the
  token, so "0 occurrences of token/JWT/PEM material in stdout and stderr"
  (grep includes the PEM's body line) is a meaningful zero.
- **Fail-soft-after-push control**: with the approve POST stubbed to 422, the
  step still exits 0, still revokes, still leaves no temp files, still writes
  the summary (0 approved).

## Figures

One line each; every command ran in `/tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-approveb` (worktree
`wt`, scratch harness `scratch/`) at the head above unless it names another
commit.

- **A — fail-soft, secret absent, committed body (e71ba6e)**: `env -u RUNS_PEM -u RUNS_APPID ... bash scratch/step_new.sh` → rc 0; stdout+stderr exactly 1 line (`::notice::HPO_RUNS_PEM is not set; leaving action_required runs for a human (fail-soft)`); summary 0 bytes; 0 temp files.
- **B — the round-1 defect reproduced (control)**: round-0 body (extracted at ca0d196), real throwaway RSA key, real openssl, curl stubbed → rc 0; first line `::warning::signing the run-approver App JWT failed; nothing approved (fail-soft)`; 0 approve POSTs; the curl stub was never invoked (no network call at all).
- **C — repaired body (e71ba6e), real key, real openssl, curl stubbed** → rc 0; stdout `approved run 111 (Tests)` / `approved run 222 (Governance)`; 2 approve POSTs, 1 token mint, 1 revoke; 0 temp files left; 0 occurrences of stub token / PEM header / PEM body line in stdout+stderr; summary block `2 run(s) ... approved by the Actions-only App` / `after-state: 0 run(s) still action_required`; the captured JWT verifies `Verified OK` against the throwaway public key with payload `iss` = 424242 (from `RUNS_APPID`) and header `RS256`.
- Fail-soft, APPID absent — committed body with `RUNS_PEM=<key> RUNS_APPID=` → rc 0, exactly 1 warning line, 0 temp files.
- Approve-refused fail-soft — stub approve POSTs return 422 → rc 0, one `::warning::approving run <id> ... was refused` per run, revoke still happens, 0 temp files.
- Listing-failure fail-soft — stub listing returns 500 → rc 0, one `::warning::listing ... failed` line, 0 approve POSTs, revoke still happens, 0 temp files.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/tests.yml'))"` → parses; `bash -n` clean on all step bodies of both jobs.
- `grep -c APPROVER .github/workflows/tests.yml` → 0; the two PEM writes now read `printf '%s\n' "$RUNS_PEM" > "$key"` (tests.yml, both approve steps).
- `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --check` → `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 39 policy file(s)`.
- `node .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs --budgets | grep ci-autofix` → `.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md  96  96` — at its cap, not over it; no cap edited.
- `wc -l .claude/rules/ci-autofix.md` → 96 (unchanged by both the sentence and the round-1 repair; the sentence fit by reflowing its paragraph's four lines, max line 107, inside the file's own 108-char table-row width).
- Rule diff is exactly one inserted sentence — word-stream check against origin/main: first divergence at word 699 of 855; deleting the 18 inserted words (`Both jobs also approve those held runs as a dedicated Actions-only App, fail-soft while its secrets are absent.`) reproduces the origin/main text word-for-word (`True`); no other word moved. The sentence names no secret (reworded at 5258bd2 from `… while \`HPO_RUNS_PEM\` is absent`); `node .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs` → `1 file(s) written` and `policy_lint --budgets` still shows 96/96.
- `node .claude/workflows/rules_sync.mjs` → `RULES-SYNC: 0 file(s) written, 10 source(s)` (the `.mdc` mirror was generated at round 0 and matches).
- `python3 tests/structure.py` → `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` → `ALL 1629 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py` → `ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED` — no D5/D6 header moved, nothing re-recorded.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` → `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out` with reason `.github/workflows/tests.yml changes the gate itself, so every closure is suspect`; no `scope.run` named, so per `fixer.md` step 5 the full suite is CI's to run. No gate lease taken.
- Claim files — `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` → empty: this branch claims nothing.

## Red checks

none red at this head locally (`structure`, `entities`, `harness_headers`,
`policy_lint --check` all green above); CI runs the full gate this branch's
diff forces (`MODE: FULL`). The branch claims nothing, so `INHERITED CLAIMS`
is not owed, and no new selectable script exists, so `UNDER-SCOPED` is not
owed either (`ci-autofix.md` naming rule).

**Round-1 block answered by name — `dead-approve-step` (#1280):** the defect
was two sites (the PEM write in each approve step, tests.yml at ca0d196
lines 1284 and 1485) writing `$APPROVER_PEM`, a variable the
`HPO_APPROVER_*` → `HPO_RUNS_*` rename had orphaned — the guards and messages
were renamed, the write was not. With real secrets the key file was one
byte, openssl refused, and every run ended at the signing-failure warning
with exit 0. **The cheaper detector that would have caught it, and its
standing cost:** one end-to-end run of the extracted step body with a REAL
throwaway RSA key (`openssl genpkey`, seconds) and only `curl` stubbed —
real openssl refuses the 1-byte key exactly as CI would have; the round-0
harness stubbed openssl too (app_approve.sh's self-test shape, which is
key-free by design) and its stub validated key-file non-emptiness only, so a
newline passed. That real-key run is now part of this body's figures (B/C
pair) and stays in `/tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-approveb/scratch/` for any reviewer
to re-run. Also repaired per the same verdict: `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP`
so the EXIT trap fires on job cancellation.

## Forward-carry

The one-sentence addition to `.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md` IS the
propagation (in this pull request, not a comment): the rule that binds every
seat that waits on these jobs now describes the approve step and its
fail-soft default. No brief or roster needs a second copy.

## Approval

Required, and recorded here: this diff touches `.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md`
(a CODEOWNERS path, `/.claude/rules/ @tvofi`), so the pull request cannot
merge without the owner's approving review on GitHub (`main-protect`'s
`require_code_owner_review`, decision 0009 step 6 — the approver App cannot
satisfy it, decision 0011). The policy change is exactly one sentence —
"Both jobs also approve those held runs as a dedicated Actions-only App,
fail-soft while its secrets are absent." — appended to the rule's
loop-guard paragraph, inside the file's 96-line cap (no cap raised); the
rest of the paragraph is rewrapped word-identically (proof in `## Figures`).
The sentence describes what the step does and its fail-soft default, and
deliberately names no secret (a secret name in policy rots on rotation).

## Friction

none

Rounds 1-2 (round 1 blocked dead-approve-step — the APPROVER_PEM orphan caught and fixed with a real-key end-to-end verification; round 2 verified the one-word fix, the INT/TERM/HUP traps, and the committed-YAML caseC: real RS256 JWT verified under openssl, 2 approve POSTs, 1 mint, 1 revoke, mode-600 headers, zero leaks, the dead step reproduced as the control). The token_push gate, the same-repo-only listing, the fail-soft semantics, and the credential discipline held under every attack. Evidence: /tmp/hpo-orch/review-1280/evidence-ca0d196/ plus the scratch harness under /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-approveb/scratch/.

p1281.title: re-record the D6 register: C28 reads the menu sentence the lift rewrote
p1281.body:
Why this change, and what it measures.

The owner asked for two changes to one menu entry (Part of #201): the pre-fill
page is renamed **"Pre-fill from a heat pump device"** — a Tuya device is the
primary source, the Modbus package secondary — and lifted out of **Advanced
settings** onto the first menu. This is a label and IA change only: the
internal step key `modbus_prefill` and the config key
`CONF_MODBUS_PREFILL_PREFIX` are unchanged, so no stored entry and no rendered
field moves; renaming either would orphan every stored entry that answered the
page. The Swedish rendering is "Förifyll från en värmepumpsenhet", the wording
the initial flow's own `device_prefill` step (strings.json:331) already
carries, so the two pre-fill surfaces now name the same thing in both
languages.

Part of #201. Closes nothing — a label/IA change, no issue.

## Head

2a766a7567f8bc802b97b246a9e9258afd18f9c2 (branch `fix/prefill-rename`,
merge base `origin/main` = `ac8b1ec`, #1280 verified merged before the
worktree was cut).

## What changed

Rename sites (old → new text "Pre-fill from a Modbus heat pump" →
"Pre-fill from a heat pump device"; sv "Förifyll från en Modbus-värmepump" →
"Förifyll från en värmepumpsenhet"):

- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/config_flow.py:1482` — the `_P`
  registry row's label, and its `menu` column `_ADVANCED` → `_TOP`, row moved
  to sit between `away` and `quick_setup` (so `quick_setup` stays the last
  top page, which its own #1258 comment and docs/setup.md:105-106 pin on
  purpose).
- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/config_flow.py:3127` — the
  `async_step_quick_setup` docstring's "the advanced Pre-fill from a Modbus
  heat pump page" → "the Pre-fill from a heat pump device page on the first
  menu" (a code comment, corrected because the lift makes the old sentence
  factually wrong, not for style).
- `strings.json` / `translations/en.json`: `options.step.init.menu_options`
  gains `modbus_prefill` (:454), `options.step.advanced.menu_options` loses
  it, `options.step.modbus_prefill.title` (:1386), and the quick_setup
  description (:1018) — "the pre-fill stays on the advanced Pre-fill from a
  Modbus heat pump page" → "the pre-fill stays on the Pre-fill from a heat
  pump device page" (wrong twice over before: "advanced" and the label).
- `translations/sv.json`: the same four sites; the quick_setup description
  drops "den avancerade sidan" for "sidan".
- `docs/setup.md:111-112` and `:200-201` — both "the advanced **Pre-fill
  from a Modbus heat pump**" mentions lose "advanced" and gain the new label.
- `docs/configuration.md` — the count sentence "seven on the first menu, and
  sixteen more behind" → "eight … fifteen more" (:205-206); the First-menu
  table gains the row (:223); the Advanced-settings table loses it; the
  section heading (:394) is renamed and the section moved to registry order
  (after Away and holiday mode), with its intro reworked to lead with the
  device route instead of the Modbus package.
- `README.md:746` — the row moves from the Advanced-page table to the Page
  table, reworded "Suggested values read from the pump's own device entities
  or a GCHV pump's Modbus package".

Group move, consequences traced and handled:

- **Return-to-menu routing** (`config_flow.py` `_save_or_menu`, the
  ":3010 advanced pages return to the advanced menu" logic): derived from the
  registry's `menu` column via `_ADVANCED_MENU`, so the lift reroutes the
  page's after-save return to the top menu with no production change; five
  `shows_menu(..., "advanced")` expectations in `tests/config_flow_steps.py`
  (the prefill save paths) flip to `"init"`, and the stale comment at the
  quick-setup save check is reworded.
- **Tests pinning the group**: `opt_init` / `opt_advanced` menu-order pins
  updated; `tests/entities.py`'s strings-vs-registry menu parity and partition
  checks are derived and stayed green unmodified.
- **`CONF_PREFILL_OFFER` (:1739)**: its user-facing label and description
  ("Offer this pre-fill at setup") name no menu and no "advanced" — they read
  correctly after the lift; no change needed. Code-comment prose mentioning
  "advanced" elsewhere stays (the :3010 comment remains true for the pages
  that are still advanced).
- **Frozen evidence left alone**: `tools/audit/round3/D5/option_doc_coverage.py`'s
  header recounts #1067's history and is not user-facing text.

## Mutation proof

Failing tests first, at the merge base (`ac8b1ec` + the two new checks only):

    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/config_flow_steps.py
    rc=1
    FAIL the pre-fill entry is labelled for any heat pump device, not only Modbus  [label=None]
    FAIL the pre-fill page sits on the first menu, off the advanced one  [init has it: False, advanced has it: True]

Mutation 1 — revert the production label only
(`_P("modbus_prefill", "Pre-fill from a heat pump device", _TOP)` → the old
"Pre-fill from a Modbus heat pump"), same command:

    rc=1
    1 of 449 checks FAILED
    FAIL the pre-fill entry is labelled for any heat pump device, not only Modbus  [label='Pre-fill from a Modbus heat pump']

Restored. Mutation 2 — revert the group only (`_TOP` → `_ADVANCED` in place),
same command:

    rc=1
    FAIL the top menu offers the revisited pages plus Quick setup and Advanced, in order
    FAIL the advanced menu lists the set-once pages, in order
    FAIL the pre-fill entry is labelled for any heat pump device, not only Modbus
    FAIL the pre-fill page sits on the first menu, off the advanced one
    FAIL null control: no Modbus entities, no suggestions, and the save writes nothing
    FAIL the save writes what was kept, never a blank or None, and not the default prefix
    FAIL the save writes what was kept, and never the transient device pick or a prefix
    FAIL the pre-fill page offers the switch, and turning it on stores it
    FAIL #1107: an untouched switch at its default is not stored by the pre-fill page

The five save-path failures are the return-to-menu reroute caught, which is
the traced consequence of the lift. Restored; full suite green (Figures).

## Null control

- The other fifteen advanced pages stay advanced: the `opt_advanced` pin
  (exact 15-page ordered list) and entities.py's
  "the top and advanced menus partition the pages exactly" /
  "the advanced submenu offers exactly the advanced pages" are green
  unmodified in the runs below; `solar_pv`'s advanced-return check
  (entities.py:10181) is green unchanged.
- The card is untouched: `node tests/card_drift.mjs` → "card_drift:
  identical in all 35 states"; `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` is
  byte-identical to main (0 diff lines, three-dot).
- The D5 doc-coverage counts did not move (fields, not page titles, are what
  it counts): every `option_doc_coverage.py` RESULT line matched its header
  with no re-record.

## Figures

All commands run from the worktree root at the head SHA unless a ref is
named; `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub` throughout (harness_headers sets its own
`tests/hastub:custom_components:tests`).

- Gate scope (re-derived after the last file changed):
  `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"`
  → `MODE: SCOPED -- 10 script(s) run, 14 scoped out.`; `stress.py` not
  named → no gate lease taken.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/config_flow_steps.py` →
  `ALL 449 checks PASSED`, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` →
  `ALL 1629 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` →
  `ALL 3012 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/env_drift.py --claims-only origin/main`
  → `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`, rc=0.
- `GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=origin/main PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/env_drift.py --all origin/main`
  → `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against origin/main`,
  `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56 committed fixture(s) still match what this tree
  computes`, rc=0.
- `GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=origin/main PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/golden.py`
  → same two verdicts, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/golden.py --record --only config_flow`
  → `recorded config_flow (136 KB)`; `git diff --numstat
  tests/golden/config_flow.json` → `4 4`; both hunks inside `_menu`
  (advanced loses the modbus_prefill pair, init gains it between away and
  quick_setup). No page schema, default or seed leaf moved.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/structure.py` →
  `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, rc=0 (no budget re-recorded or raised).
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` at the head and at
  `ac8b1ec` (detached worktree) → `ALL 6 typing-ruler source checks PASSED`
  both ways, rc=0. The mypy census is not run here: no pinned interpreter on
  this seat (`HPO_TYPING_PYTHON` unset, `uv`/`mypy` absent); it is checked by
  CI's `typing` job.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/deployment_shape.py` →
  `ALL DEPLOYMENT SHAPE CHECKS PASSED`, rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/plan_view.py` →
  `plan reason codes, price provenance and slot energy OK`, rc=0.
- `node tests/card_drift.mjs` → `card_drift: identical in all 35 states`,
  rc=0.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py`
  (always-on, outside the closures) → `ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`,
  rc=0, after the D6 register re-record below.
- D6 register: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3
  tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.py` regenerates
  `tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.md` + `claims.json`; exactly one row moved —
  C28's label and pair `seven/(7, 16)` → `eight/(8, 15)`, verdict still
  **true** (`git diff --numstat` over the two files: 1/1 and 2/2); every
  claims.py header aggregate matched with no header edit. D5 needed no
  re-record (null control above).
- Branch footprint, three-dot:
  `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` → 12 files, 142 insertions, 96

p1284.body:
The autofix approve step (#1280) races GitHub's run creation: it lists
`action_required` runs the instant the push step ends, but the new SHA's
`pull_request` runs are created asynchronously — measured on #1282's bot
commit `317d46e6`, the step concluded success with zero runtime output while
all five runs appeared moments later and sat held. This teaches the step to
wait for the runs it exists to approve: the push step exports the SHA it
pushed, and the approve step re-lists every 5s for up to 60s until one
`action_required` run sits at that SHA before the existing
list→approve→re-list flow, which is untouched. Expiry stays fail-soft — one
notice naming the timeout plus the after-state it always printed — because a
genuinely run-less push is legitimate (nothing-staged paths exit before
`token_push`).

Closes #1283

## Head

`b0b602d8406837cdcb0322ecb5c68265e7a7520f` (all figures below measured at
this head; merge-base with `origin/main` is `f50dcc90`, 2026-09-20T14:19:39Z,
so figures that are a function of main's tip name that tip).

## Mutation proof

`.github/workflows/tests.yml` has no local suite — no `tests/*.py` script
imports a workflow — so the failing-first instrument is a stub harness that
runs **the step body extracted from the committed YAML** (a PyYAML walk to
`jobs.<job>.steps[name="Approve the runs the push left holding"].run`), with
`curl` stubbed and everything else real: `openssl` signs a real throwaway
RSA key through the step's own mint block, `python3` parses listings, the
summary lands in a scratch `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

The stub's staging rule (the rule that produced every count below): listing
calls are numbered; 1–3 return `{"workflow_runs":[]}` (GitHub has created
nothing yet), 4–6 add only a run at an OLD sha (id 554999,
`aaaa…`, `head_sha != PUSH_SHA` — the poll must not stop on it), 7+ add the
run at the pushed SHA (id 555001). Approved ids leave the listing, as an
approved run leaves `action_required`. Every call is logged with a
timestamp. Both jobs' committed bodies are byte-identical except the summary
header (verified below), so the scenarios run `closures-autofix`'s.

Red — the pre-fix body (extracted from `origin/main`'s blob) against that
stub, i.e. the fix deleted:

    /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/harness/run-scenario.sh red-round0 \
      /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/round0-tests.yml staged closures-autofix

    --- stub call log
    16:12:43 GET .../actions/runs?...&status=action_required listing #1 -> {empty}
    16:12:44 GET .../actions/runs listing #2 -> {empty}
    16:12:44 GET .../actions/runs listing #3 -> {empty}
    --- step stdout
    (empty — zero bytes)
    --- step summary
    0 run(s) on some-branch approved by the Actions-only App
    after-state: 0 run(s) still action_required

Exit 0, one listing, nothing approved, no notice: the reproduced bug — the
stub's runs (which its rule produces from listing 4 on) were never seen, and
the summary claims a clean after-state anyway.

Green — the committed body (`git show b0b602d8:.github/workflows/tests.yml`)
against the same stub:

    /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/harness/run-scenario.sh green-fixed \
      /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/fixed-tests.yml staged closures-autofix

    --- stub call log (abridged; full log in the scenario dir)
    16:12:49 listing #1 -> {empty}
    16:12:54 listing #2 -> {empty}
    16:12:59 listing #3 -> {empty}
    16:13:05 listing #4 -> {554999}          <- old-sha run only: poll keeps waiting
    16:13:10 listing #5 -> {554999}
    16:13:15 listing #6 -> {554999}
    16:13:20 listing #7 -> {554999 555001}   <- pushed-SHA run exists: poll ends
    16:13:20 listing #8 -> {554999 555001}   <- the existing flow's own listing
    16:13:20 POST .../runs/554999/approve
    16:13:20 POST .../runs/555001/approve
    16:13:20 listing #9 -> {empty}
    16:13:20 listing #10 -> {empty}
    --- step stdout
    approved run 554999 (Tests / fast (old push))
    approved run 555001 (Tests / fast)
    --- step summary
    2 run(s) on some-branch approved by the Actions-only App
    after-state: 0 run(s) still action_required

The poll waited (6 sleeps × 5s ≈ 31s of listings 5s apart), keyed on the
pushed SHA (listings 4–6 held only the old-sha run and did not end it), then
the untouched list→approve→re-list flow ran exactly as before — it still
approves every held run on the branch, old sha included, and prints the same
summary shape.

Mutation form: the red run IS the round-0 body, the fix deleted; no
production line of the fix survives it.

## Null control

Timing/waiting claims above are controlled by the red run's call log: the
unmodified body makes exactly 3 listing calls (initial + two after-state) at
16:12:43–16:12:44 — no wait — versus the fixed body's 10 listings spanning
16:12:49–16:13:20 under the same stub and the same staging rule.

The 60s-expiry path (fail-soft, not red) is its own control: the same
committed body against a stub whose listings never produce a run
(`STUB_MODE=always-empty`):

    /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/harness/run-scenario.sh timeout-empty \
      /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/fixed-tests.yml always-empty closures-autofix

    --- stub call log
    16:13:29 listing #1 -> {empty}
    16:13:35 listing #2 -> {empty}
    ... 13 poll listings, 5s apart, through ...
    16:14:30 listing #13 -> {empty}      <- waited=60, window expires
    16:14:30 listing #14 -> {empty}      <- the flow proceeds as today
    16:14:30 listing #15 -> {empty}
    16:14:30 listing #16 -> {empty}
    --- step stdout
    ::notice::no action_required run at 317d46e6a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9a appeared within 60s of the push; printing the after-state (fail-soft)
    --- step summary
    0 run(s) on some-branch approved by the Actions-only App
    after-state: 0 run(s) still action_required

Exit 0; exactly one notice, naming the timeout; the after-state prints
exactly as the pre-fix step printed it. The 13-listing count is the rule's,
not luck: listings fire at waited=0,5,…,60 (12 sleeps × 5s = 60s window,
16:13:29→16:14:30 measured).

## Figures

- Instrument: the stub harness (`/tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/harness/`:
  `bin/curl`, `extract_step.py`, `run-scenario.sh`); scope: the
  `closures-autofix` approve-step body extracted from the committed YAML at
  `b0b602d8`, and the same extraction from `origin/main` (`f50dcc90`) for
  red. Transcripts: `/tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/scenarios/{red-round0,green-fixed,timeout-empty}/`.
- Both jobs carry the same step; the committed bodies differ only in the
  summary header line:
  `python3 /tmp/hpo-orch/fixer-1283/harness/extract_step.py <yaml> <job>` for
  each job, then `diff` — one hunk: `### closures-autofix:` vs
  `### claims-autofix:`.
- Push-step wiring: `steps.push.outputs.pushed_sha` is
  `echo "pushed_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`, set only on
  the `token_push` path (after `git push`, so it is the SHA that landed);
  `PUSH_SHA: ${{ steps.push.outputs.pushed_sha }}` added to both approve
  steps' env. Verified by the PyYAML walk used for extraction (`env` and
  push-step assertions) and by inspection at `.github/workflows/tests.yml`.
- Claim files byte-identical (branch claims nothing):
  `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat -- tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt`
  — no output.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` — rc=0, ALL 1629
  ENTITY CHECKS PASSED.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/structure.py` — rc=0, STRUCTURE
  RATCHET PASSED (no new file, no Python line added).
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py`
  — rc=0, ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED (no EXPECTED line reads the
  workflow file; nothing to re-record).
- Gate scope:
  `D=$(mktemp -d); PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"`
  — `MODE: FULL -- every test script runs, nothing is scoped out.` with
  reason "`.github/workflows/tests.yml` changes the gate itself, so every
  closure is suspect"; `scope.run` names nothing, so nothing is run locally
  and the full suite is CI's (a workflow-only diff cannot move a Python
  closure; the mode line's reason says exactly this).

## Red checks

none locally (no check ran red on this branch; CI's `MODE: FULL` run is the
remaining arbiter).

## Forward-carry

none — `.claude/rules/ci-autofix.md` describes the approve step's inputs and
fail-soft contract, neither of which changed (no new job was added; the
existing step gained a bounded wait), so no brief or rule text went stale.
The orchestrator-side `tools/audit/approve_held_runs.sh` (#1279) already
covers every merge and is untouched. Delivery row: `docs/delivery/<N>.md` is
owed once this pull request's number exists (delivery-status-tracking.md),
which is post-push and the orchestrator's moment.

## Friction

p1286.body:
<!-- pr-body for fix/plan-history; validated with tools/audit/prepr.sh before handoff -->
Why this change, and what it measures.

The owner asked for the plan figure in the dashboard card to pan BACK through
history — up to 48 hours — showing the actual (recorded) temperatures, prices,
solar irradiance and actioned slots in place of the plan's forward-looking
series while the user pans. This branch implements it entirely in the card
(no integration Python is touched): `ViewWindow`'s left bound extends to
`now - 48 h` while a `hass.callApi` exists, a new `HistorySource`
collaborator lazily fetches the recorder's past in epoch-aligned 12 h
windows as the pan enters them, and the measured samples ride the plan's own
series left of the existing "now" rule, which stays the seam. The pump's own
commanded power is a new eighth series ("Actioned power", kW, teal #00838f,
same power axis as the planned slot bars), because no plan series honestly
carries it: the action covers both circuits and the plan splits them.

Owner-requested work; closes nothing. Part of #201.

## Head

90177d280a0905c3a7b5c671e1c29f70bfbad1fd (merge base f50dcc9, origin/main at
branch time; #1282 `fix/polish-every-candidate` was NOT merged then — if it
merges before this branch lands and the card conflicts, that absorb is the
orchestrator's merge-prep, not this branch's).

The four design decisions, each with its why:

(a) **Data source — Home Assistant's history API, states not statistics.**
`hass.callApi("GET", "history/period/<start>?filter_entity_id=...&end_time=...")`
against the integration's own actual-carrying sensors:
`sensor.<prefix>_indoor_temperature_optimizer` (measured indoor -> the house
temperature series), `sensor.<prefix>_outdoor_temperature_optimizer` (measured
outdoor), `sensor.<prefix>_cost_current_electricity_price` (the spot price the
plan was actually priced against), the resolved solar entity
(`solar_entity` config / `plan_kind` discovery / `_solar_irradiance` suffix ->
`ghi`), and `sensor.<prefix>_heat_pump_action` (the actioned record). Ids are
derived from the RESOLVED plan sensor's prefix exactly the way the card
already derives its headline stat sensors since #1227 (suffix replacement,
then a sorted scan for hand-renamed entities) — measured by the
"a renamed install derives its own actual sensors" check against a
`sensor.villa_*` install. States rather than statistics because the plan chart
plots point series — a mean/min/max bucket is a different claim than "what the
sensor said at 12:03" — and the price is a step function. Payload, measured on
the rig's HA-shaped stub at the integration's default 30-minute cadence
(`DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL`, const.py; the recorder stores state CHANGES,
so this is the ceiling): the four numeric entities over the full 48 h with
`minimal_response&no_attributes` serialize to 22123 bytes, the action entity
with attributes to 10408 bytes — about 32 KiB for everything, roughly 8 KiB
per 12 h chunk, and a quick 10-minute glance back costs one chunk.

(b) **The pan interaction — the existing machinery, one bound extended.**
`ViewWindow.apply` gains a fourth argument, the history left bound; `floor`
stays the default start (now) because `current()` reads it as the untouched
window, and a new `limits.leftBound` is what the pan clamps against, so an
untouched card renders exactly as before. The bound is optimistic — it
extends as soon as `callApi` exists — and retracts the moment the recorder
answers nothing, at which point the next build's clamp snaps the window back
to the live edge; the reset button remains the explicit snap-back. Chunks are
epoch-aligned 12 h windows fetched from `_buildSeries` when the visible window
enters them (the pan itself caused that render), deduplicated by a chunk map,
so nothing fetches until a pan actually crosses now and a fast drag across 48 h
costs four windows, not one giant one. What the user sees: left of the now
rule (which draws whenever it is in window, as it always did) the measured
traces in the same series, colours and axes their forecasts occupy right of
it — the seam is the now rule, and the forecast is cut at the live edge under
history so past and plan never double-book a timestamp (pinned by the
"never double-book" check; the plan payload's own first steps predate the
solve and would otherwise collide with measured samples in a test fixture).

(c) **Actioned slots — the heat_pump_action sensor's own history.** It is the
integration's record of what it commanded at each moment — the mode as the
state and the commanded power in the `power_kw` attribute — whereas the plan
sensors' `slots` attribute history is what was PLANNED as of each moment (and
the plan sensors keep `forecast` out of the recorder precisely because
superseded plans are noise). So the action sensor is authoritative for "what
was actioned"; its `power_kw` draws as the Actioned power step bars on the
same axis as the planned slots, and an install that publishes no power in
`current_action` gets an empty series whose chip reads nodata — the same
convention as solar without a solar entity. The action entity is fetched in
its own call WITHOUT `no_attributes` (its value lives in an attribute), apart
from the lean numeric call — pinned by the "the action call carries the
attributes its power lives in" check.

(d) **Card states and claims.** The rig gained `historyApi` (a `callApi` stub
that PARSES the path the card built — start, `end_time`, `filter_entity_id`,
`minimal_response`/`no_attributes` — and serves HA-shaped arrays from a
deterministic 48 h fixture at 30-minute cadence with one mid-window
`unavailable` sample), `historyFixture`, `withActuals` (the actual sensors as
hass.states knows them — a real install has them beside the plan sensors, and
the card's derivation checks presence first) and `flushHistory`.
`card_drift.mjs`'s `renderAll` awaits the (possibly async) drive functions so
a state can let its fetch land before the tree is read, and four new states
join the roster: `history_panned`, `history_deep_panned`,
`history_unavailable`, `history_pending`. All 39 states move and all 39 are
claimed in `tests/golden/card_claimed_drift.txt` with directions: the 35
pre-existing states move by exactly one mechanism each — the eighth legend
chip (measured: the only removed line in each of the 34 legend-bearing
states' diffs is the legend node's own html string, rewritten to insert the
chip; `editor_schema` gains the one series toggle in its JSON) — and the four
new states are the feature itself. `claims-for:` stays at the live VERSION
6.6.6.

(e) **Backend — none; pure card work.** No published attribute was needed: the
actuals' ids are derivable by the suffix pattern the card already trusts for
its stat sensors, and `setup_topology` carries the USER'S input entities, not
the optimizer's own sensors, so it is the wrong source for these. A new
`history_entities` attribute would grow every plan payload to restate what a
stable naming rule already answers. The one deliberate non-config: the 48 h
span is a constant (`HISTORY_SPAN_MS`), not a YAML key, so the editor schema,
D5/D6 config tables and the harness headers are untouched by new config
surface.

## Mutation proof

Failing first, at the merge base f50dcc9 with only the tests applied:
`node tests/card.mjs` printed `18 CARD CHECK(S) FAILED` — every history check
("panning back before now moves the window into the past", the four
"the measured <x> renders left of now", "panning back stops at 48 hours",
"the actioned series has a legend chip", both degrade-to-notice checks, the
lean-call and entity-derivation checks) plus the two deliberately updated
legend-count checks ("legend has all eight series", "the legend still carries
one chip per series"). The same tree without the tests passes
(`ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`).

Mutation 1 — the pan-back clamp: `const start = clampNum(this.range.start,
leftBound, maxStart)` mutated to clamp at `defaultStart` instead (the 48 h
bound deleted, the tail untouched). `node tests/card.mjs`:
`16 CARD CHECK(S) FAILED`, including `panning back stops at 48 hours before
now` and `panning back before now moves the window into the past`. Restored.

Mutation 2 — the lazy-fetch wiring: `this.histSource.ensure(view.start,
dw.start);` deleted from `_buildSeries`. `node tests/card.mjs`:
`15 CARD CHECK(S) FAILED`, including all four `the measured <indoor|outdoor|
spot price|irradiance> renders left of now`, `history loads lazily`, both
`history <recorder off|api refused> degrades to a notice` checks and the
renamed-install derivation check. Restored; `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`.

One check was strengthened because the mutation proved it vacuous: keyed on
`t < now` it still passed under mutation 2, satisfied by the plan payload's
own pre-solve steps; it now demands points strictly left of the forecast's
first step, and goes red under the mutation.

## Null control

- A hass WITHOUT `callApi` keeps the forward-only pan exactly as before the
  feature (`a hass without callApi keeps the forward-only pan`), and the
  pre-existing item-23 block still passes unchanged on such a hass.
- The recorder answering nothing (recorder off / entities excluded / purged)
  and the API refusing both degrade to a `role="status"` notice over the live
  view, snap the window back to now, and never throw — two checks, both arms.
- Panning FORWARD past the plan still stops at the plan's end, with history
  loaded and without (`panning forward still stops at the end of the plan`).
- An untouched card never issues a history call — zero fetches by render.
- The docs figures: regenerated at the merge base and at this head in one
  environment, both card figures come out byte-identical (diff of the two
  regenerations: 0 lines) — this change moves neither, because the figures
  draw the chart body, not the legend chips, and a render without a recorder
  stub has no history to draw.
- The palette's own floors absorb the new series colour unchanged: the
  existing D4-08 (3:1 on #ffffff and #1c1c1c) and #558 C1 (deuteranope dE
  >= 10 overall, >= 20 within a shared draw style unless dashed) checks are
  SERIES_DEFS-driven and passed without modification; #00838f measures 4.52:1
  light, 3.77:1 dark, minimum dE 12.6 to any series, 37.8 to space_slots and
  60.6 to dhw_slots — no dash needed.

## Figures

- Failing-first at base (tests only): `node tests/card.mjs` ->
  `18 CARD CHECK(S) FAILED`; clean base control: `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`.
- Final: `node tests/card.mjs` -> `ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED` (912 ok checks);
  rc=0.
- Markup gate: `node tests/card_drift.mjs origin/main` -> `card_drift: 39
  state(s) moved and claimed, 0 identical`; rc=0.
- Scoped gate at the merge base: `GATE_SCOPE=auto GATE_SCOPE_BASE=$(git
  merge-base origin/main HEAD) bash tests/run.sh` -> `MODE: SCOPED -- 8
  script(s) run, 16 scoped out`, `10 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 16 SCOPED OUT AND
  NOT RUN`; rc=0.
- Structure: `python3 tests/structure.py` -> `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`;
  rc=0. No budget was raised, re-recorded or paid: the card is JavaScript and
  no coordinator-scoped metric moved (the owner's standing pre-approval for
  this feature's raises was therefore not needed).
- Always-on header gate: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3
  tests/harness_headers.py` -> `ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; rc=0.
- D6 register: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3
  tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.py` -> `claims_true=123`, C85 true again after
  docs/dashboard-card.md documents the eighth key; rc=0.
- Real-browser layout lane (its own CI job's command, Playwright installed
  locally): `NODE_PATH=<pwlane>/node_modules node tests/card_browser.mjs` ->
  `ALL BROWSER CHECKS PASSED`; rc=0 — the eighth chip wraps
  (`.legend` is `flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px`) and passes the chip-overlap and
  label-fit checks.
- History payload, measured on the rig's HA-shaped stub at the 30-minute
  default cadence over the full 48 h: numeric call (4 entities,
  `minimal_response&no_attributes`) 22123 bytes; action call with attributes
  10408 bytes; ~8 KiB per 12 h chunk. Rule: cadence DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL
  = 30 min and the recorder stores changes only, so this is the ceiling.

## Red checks

`tests/harness_headers.py: the executed harnesses leave their committed

p1285.body:
<!-- Fixer seat for #1230. Merge base / origin/main tip at measurement time:
     f50dcc90e57c (stamped 2026-09-20T14:43Z; every figure below is a
     function of that tip and of the head SHA in ## Head). -->

Closes #1230

Why this change, and what it measures.

Issue #1230 (round-5 D9-02, judge weakened/low): `_apply_dhw_min_run`
re-simulated the whole horizon once per weak slot (twice when the raise was
refused), so a repair over `w` weak slots of an `n`-step horizon cost about
`w*(n+1)` simulate steps through `simulate_dhw_only` — the 4.02x horizon
scaling the finder measured. The fix is the incremental shape the issue
proposes: a raise at slot `i` cannot change any state before it, so the
candidate's trajectory shares the current plan's prefix exactly, and the
check — and the zero-refresh on a refusal — now extend the current
trajectory from the slot's own start state through the production
`extend_dhw_temps` seam (`thermal_model.py`, already exercised by the W3-G2
pin). The same step function runs in the same order on the same values, so
every accept/refuse decision and the resulting plan are bit-identical to the
full replay's; only the skipped prefix work differs. Honest scope of the
win, stated exactly: `simulate_dhw_only` calls per repair drop from
`2 + w (+ refusals)` to exactly 2, and the simulate-step work drops from
`w*(n+1)*(1+refusal fraction)` to `sum_j (n - pos_j) * (1 + refusal_j)` —
suffix work only, about half the old count for spread weak slots and
shrinking to zero for late ones. The worst case (all weak slots at the very
start of the horizon) is still linear-in-`w` suffix work per slot; this is a
constant-factor and call-count fix on steps, a call-count elimination on the
finder's instrument, and it removes the quadratic *horizon* scaling the
issue measured (4.02x -> 2.00x on the finder's own harness, below).

## Head

5ac42f21633ee059dc32fd891d019020deeb2fe5 (merge base f50dcc90e57c).
Every measurement below was taken at that tree. The scoped gate was
executed on a local measurement branch = this head plus one commit that
previews exactly what the `claims-autofix` bot writes (`ci: drop inherited
claims`, empty claim list); that edit touches `tests/golden/
claimed_drift.txt` only and affects no measured behaviour — the same
`env_drift.py --all` verdict (56/56 byte-identical, no stale fixture) was
taken on both trees.

## Mutation proof

Hand mutation (the fixer contract's revert), production file only, restore
verified by re-running the carrier:

- reverted `_apply_dhw_min_run`'s loop to the per-slot whole-horizon replay
  (`raised = plan.copy()` + `trajectory(raised)` per slot) at head,
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` -> rc=1,
  `3 of 3019 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`, the three reds being exactly the new
  pins: `simulate_dhw_only calls stay at 2 as weak slots double
  (12 -> 24 -> 48 weak slots)` [got 24-slot 34, 12-slot 17, 48-slot 66],
  `simulate_dhw_step calls stay inside the incremental ceiling (2 sims +
  suffix work from each weak slot)` [24-slot 3264/2544, 12-slot 1632,
  48-slot 12672], `a single weak slot is decided in at most three
  trajectories` [calls 4]. Restored (head 5ac42f2 re-applied byte-for-byte,
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` -> rc=0,
  `ALL 3019 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`). Baseline red run before the fix
  existed: same rc=1, same three names, same numbers.

Committed mutation, in-tree and permanent (features.py, #1230 section): a
wrapper reroutes `extend_dhw_temps` through `simulate_dhw_only` whole-horizon
replay — per-slot replay restored through the production seam, with the
W3-G2 unpatch/repatch dance because `simulate_dhw_only` itself delegates
into `extend_dhw_temps`. Under the fix (measured at head): fixed
calls=2 steps=1967 (ceiling 2544) vs mutant calls=36 steps=3264, plan bytes
identical — the wrapper reds both scaling pins while moving nothing.

## Null control

- A plan with no weak slot does no simulation at all: 0 `simulate_dhw_only`
  calls, 0 `simulate_dhw_step` calls, output `np.clip(plan, 0, p_max)`
  (features.py pin; both ends green — the fix does not touch that path).
- A single weak slot: decided in 2 trajectories at head (3 allowed; the
  baseline needed 4), output byte-identical to the full-replay wrapper's
  (features.py pin, mutation-control clause).
- The finder's own null arm `two_zone_nodhw` (DHW off): dhw_steps=0,
  dhw_calls=0, dhw_plan_calls=0 at BOTH the merge base and head — the fix
  adds no work where the site never ran.
- Planner-invocation control, both finder arms: `dhw_plan_calls=2` at
  24 h and 48 h, base and head — the step-count drop is not a changed
  invocation count.
- Whole-solve identity beyond the fixtures: 240-configuration direct-drive
  parity sweep (n in {24,96,192} steps, weak slots {1,6,24,48}, seeds {0,7},
  initial temp {44,50,55} C, ceiling {44,50} C, min_run {0.6,1.2} kW),
  per-arm module resolution printed and verified: 0 mismatches, byte-exact.
- Solver effort unchanged: finder `solver_evals` 610 (24 h) / 1050 (48 h)
  at base and head alike.

## Figures

Instruments: the finder's #1230 harness (`tools/audit/round5/D9/
solve_cost.py`, recovered verbatim from `origin/audit/round5-harnesses` at
e7be4d14cbc7, run per its header from each tree's root); a direct-drive
counter bench hooking the production symbols `ThermalModel.
simulate_dhw_only` / `simulate_dhw_step` around `_apply_dhw_min_run`; and an
interleaved A/B wall/CPU bench (3 runs per arm per figure, arms alternated
process-by-process, each arm's module resolution printed; CPU ~ wall on
every line, single-threaded). Box: Apple M1, shared — two other seats
active, `load1` between 4.1 and 7.6 across the measurements
(`RESULT thread_factor=0.999`, swapins=0 in both finder runs); the gate
lease (`fixer-1230-timing`, tests/gate_lock.py) was held for every timing
and gate run below. Counts are contention-immune; wall/CPU medians carry
their spreads.

- Finder harness, merge base f50dcc9 vs head 5ac42f2 (same commands):
  `two_zone_dhw` dhw_steps 11328 -> 2304, dhw_calls 118 -> 24;
  `hours_48` dhw_steps 42624 -> 5568, dhw_calls 222 -> 29;
  site-attributed `trajectory` steps 9408 -> 384 (24 h) and 37824 -> 768
  (48 h); the finder's quadratic signal — `trajectory`-site scaling
  24 h -> 48 h — is 4.02x at base and 2.00x at head.
- Direct-drive counts at head (counter bench, fixture = 24 of 96 / 48 of
  192 weak slots, both loop branches exercised: 16 raised, 8 zeroed):
  (96,24) simulate_dhw_only calls 34 -> 2, simulate_dhw_step calls
  3264 -> 1967; (96,12) 17 -> 2 calls, 1632 -> 1006 steps;
  (192,48) 66 -> 2 calls, 12672 -> 7391 steps. Derived incremental
  ceiling for (96,24): 2544.
- Wall/CPU, direct drive, median of 3 (per-rep medians in parentheses):
  (96,24) base 14.17 ms (13.79/14.17/14.31, spread 13.56-14.36) vs head
  8.07 ms (8.07/8.08/8.04, spread 8.03-8.35) — 1.75x;
  (192,48) base 53.94 ms (53.94/54.42/51.93, spread 52.64-56.95) vs head
  30.02 ms (31.66/30.02/29.96, spread 29.92-32.12) — 1.80x.
- Whole-solve wall/CPU (3 runs, same interleave): 24 h base 1585 vs head
  1615 CPU ms, 48 h base 5885 vs head 6384 CPU ms — inside load noise
  (spreads overlap; the site is ~2% of a 48 h solve), so the whole-solve
  claim rests on the step counts above, not on these medians.
- Plan identity: `GOLDEN_REF=f50dcc9 DRIFT_NO_CACHE=1 PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub
  python3 tests/env_drift.py --all` on the measurement tree -> rc=0,
  `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked`, `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56
  committed fixture(s) still match what this tree computes`.
- Structure/typing: `python3 tests/structure.py` rc=0 at base and head with
  byte-identical ok-lines; `python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` rc=0 at base and
  head (source scan; no `# type: ignore` added); `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:
  custom_components:tests python3 tests/harness_headers.py` -> rc=0,
  `ALL 91 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3
  tests/entities.py` -> rc=0, `ALL 1629 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`.
- Scoped gate on the measurement tree (post-bot preview):
  `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff f50dcc9` -> `MODE: SCOPED -- 20
  script(s) run, 4 scoped out`; then
  `HPO_GATE_LOCK_LABEL=fixer-1230-timing GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift
  GOLDEN_REF=f50dcc9 ./tests/run.sh` -> rc=0,
  `22 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED; 4 SCOPED OUT AND NOT RUN`
  (frontend.py, ha_contract.py, harness_headers.py, open_meteo.py — each
  "no changed file is in its measured closure"; harness_headers was also
  run standalone at head: rc=0, 91 checks). stress.py ran alone under the
  lease on the loaded box: `ALL 68 STRESS CHECKS PASSED`.

## Red checks

- `INHERITED CLAIMS` (tests/env_drift.py, on this branch before the bot
  commit): named, per ci-autofix.md — `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` here
  is byte-identical to origin/main's (this diff claims nothing and moves
  nothing, so the file is untouched by this branch); `claims-autofix`
  pushes `ci: drop inherited claims` on the PR and the dispatched recheck
  runs the gate. Locally previewed that exact edit on the measurement tree:
  env_drift rc=0 and the scoped gate rc=0 quoted above.
- `typing` CI job (pinned mypy census): no local pinned interpreter exists
  (no `uv` on this box); the typing_ruler source ratchet is green at both
  ends and the diff adds no annotations and no ignores.

## Forward-carry

none — the harness trap this seat hit (out-of-tree drivers importing
`tests/golden.py` from a foreign cwd silently measure the main checkout,
because golden.py inserts `custom_components` relative to cwd) is already
documented policy at `tools/audit/README.md` ("It runs from the repository
root ... `tests/harness.py` inserts relative paths, `tests/golden.py` opens
`tests/golden/` relatively"); this seat's scratch benches were re-run
per-arm-cwd with printed module resolution.

# fix(#1208): polish every solved candidate inside the loop — UNBOUNDED, budgets raised to measured values, the two ruled movers may-drifted

Implements #1208 (round-5 D0-02) in the UNBOUNDED form on the owner's
override (#1208 comment 5748462577, 2026-09-20, verbatim: *"But I want you
to implement it with budget raise."*), with every gate the branch refuses
raised only to its measured value at this branch's own base, and — per the
owner's ruling on the stop-rule's options (#1208 comment 208bed25,
in-session "A", option (a)) — the two in-band movers carried as scoped
may-drift entries with their removal condition.

Why this change, and what it measures.

## Head

`8e3dc89889e0c21a04abf1f3be51f3776510042f` (repair round 1 on top of the
bot head 317d46e; merge base
f50dcc90 — the base CI's drift gate compares against). Earlier figures
executed at e73bda3/24e2fca on this box (darwin 25.6.0 arm64, load1 5–10,
thread factor 1.000 on every stress run); the CI-red repairs were measured
from the runner's own log (job 106089813679, run 35513807864).

## Repair round 1 (CI reds at the bot head 317d46e)

Two real failures, both answered:

**(1) 1 UNCLAIMED DRIFT vs f50dcc90 — a third mover, `shoulder_two_zone`.**
The runner (judge of record) saw `DRIFT shoulder_two_zone: 452 leaves
moved vs f50dcc90`; the dev box saw it byte-identical (the local
50-fixture dump moved only flat_prices and winter_two_zone_no_dhw), so
the move is runner-conditional exactly like the ruled pair. The runner's
own printed leaves: `deferred_energy_cost: -0.274173 vs -0.464963`,
`displace_schedule[12..15]` shifted by 0.3–1.0 of ~14–18-valued steps —
452 of the payload's leaves moved. Magnitude, from the one money leaf the
log prints: |−0.274173 − (−0.464963)| = 0.190790 against the committed
fixture's predicted_cost 8.711737 = **2.19e-2 relative — at, and by 10 %
over, the noise band's 2e-2 top edge**; the canonical scalar
(predicted_cost itself) was not among the four printed leaves, so the
in/out-of-band call cannot be made cleanly from the log. One more
measured fact for the owner: the branch side (−0.274173) matches the
committed recording (−0.269921, rel 4.9e-4) — it is the runner's
UNPOLISHED baseline capture that sits in the outlier basin; the polish
moved the runner's solve ONTO the recording machine's answer. Verdict:
borderline at the band's top edge on the one measurable leaf — surfaced
to the owner, who **ruled (i): a third may-drift name is sanctioned**
(#1208 comment fd13246 / database id 5750673720 records the options and
the numbers; the in-session ruling chose (i)). Executed in commit
8e3dc89: `shoulder_two_zone` joins the may-drift entries in the same
shape with the same removal conditions, `RUNNER_CONDITIONAL_1208`
extends to exactly three names, and the entities widening pin's set
equality moved with it — a fourth name in the constant is an unruled
widening. Re-verified at the merge base f50dcc90: `env_drift
--claims-only` rc=0; `env_drift --all` — NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT (56
checked), NO STALE FIXTURE, the two dev-box movers read MAY-DRIFT
plan-only (524/535 leaves) and shoulder_two_zone reads may-drift
did-not-move-here (the entry asserts nothing either way; the runner
that moves it is covered).

**(2) 2 of 68 stress fails — the localised-regression pair at the
runner-measured 1.80x.** `winter/tariff+cycle` and `winter/tariff+pv+cycle`
at 906/504 = 1.80x solver evaluations and 4219392/2347584 = 1.80x
simulate step-equivalents, on an UNCHANGED plan (objective 218.3908665
both sides), over the dev-measured 1.73 factor — the runner's float
environment makes the polish loop iterate more on those two bimodal
scenarios, the same cross-platform iterate-path variance the factor's
original 1.5-vs-1.05 sizing reserved slack for. Answered by raising
`SCENARIO_WORK_FACTOR` 1.73 → **1.80**, to the runner-measured value and
no further (commit d9cf13e; owner authorization: the #1208
budget-raise instruction covers the measured value wherever the gate is
measured; 1.80 < DETECTION_TARGET 2.0, so the single-scenario 2x
detection still binds on both channels). Re-run under the gate lease at
the raised head, against the same merge base CI uses (f50dcc90):
**ALL 68 STRESS CHECKS PASSED** — solver work judged at the 1.80x factor,
46 of 51 covered, 5 re-planned, worst scenario 1052.4x against the
1630x live budget; the localised pair passes and nothing else moved
(stress-180.log). Cheap re-stamps at the same head: entities ALL 1630
PASS, structure PASSED, typing source-only ALL 6 PASS, harness_headers
ALL 91 PASS, env_drift --claims-only origin/main rc=0.

**(3)** The pr-contract failure was this body not naming the reds — this
section names them; both answers above.

## The fix

`optimizer.py:_multi_start_minimize` now calls `_lbfgsb_restart` inside the
candidate loop, on every solved candidate, at the full restart budget, and
ships the cross-candidate minimum; the post-loop restart on the raw-best
result is gone. This is the parked a42e961 #1208 hunk (the UNBOUNDED
variant — the only one without the jac-parity break the #1272 capped
variants showed), adapted to a base without #1207 (the keep-gate stays at
main's 2e-2) and without #1210 (PR #1276 is still open; nothing of it is
duplicated here).

## Mutation proof

`optimizer.py`, i.e. the fix reverted — `git show HEAD~1:...optimizer.py`),

(A first mutation attempt spliced the region by hand and died on an

## The mover ruling (#996 stop-rule → owner ruling 208bed25, option (a))

| winter_two_zone_no_dhw | −1.3365e-03 | +8.3904e-03 | both IN band |
